text: I see some conflicting information in your records, so let's start fresh. I need to understand your wrist pain better; can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and how it started?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome.

The history of right thumb and wrist pain radiating to the elbow, worsened by holding an infant (repetitive flexion/extension), and alleviated by ice is highly suggestive of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome. Your history of falling on your outstretched hand may have caused a previous fracture or ligament injury contributing to current symptoms. Do you experience any numbness or tingling in your fingers, particularly at night?
